new_issues.title: _collect_turns returns partial text as success when the stream ends before the dispatch's own result and no background agent is tracked.
new_issues.why: True at head: when result is None and the ledger is empty, _collect_turns returns turns.text() with no log, even if own_result_seen is false. The comment calls this 'today's behavior', and base's dispatch likewise returned the joined text whenever receive_response() ended, result or not. The diff rewrote the loop and added a raise only for the tracked-agent case; the untracked case is carried over unchanged.

new_issues.title: Comments in _dispatch_via_agent and the summary action still say telemetry is empty when no tools ran, though prompt/settings keys are now always present.
new_issues.why: dispatch.py:612-613 still says tool_telemetry is empty with no tools, while one_shot_dispatch_with_telemetry's docstring now says the prompt and settings keys are always present. The finding also repeats the 'not reported' vs 'not computed' wording (932-I18). Comment drift only; behavior is correct.

new_issues.title: The settings-policy test helper wraps the path in contextlib.suppress(Exception).
new_issues.why: True: _capture_config suppresses every exception, with a comment explaining that paths wrap the _Captured stop in their own error types. The helper then asserts exactly one config reached the provider, so a path that fails before the provider is still caught; at worst a later unrelated error is hidden. Test-code style point.

new_issues.title: The session-path system_prompt guard checks truthiness, so an explicit empty system_prompt passes and the session prompt is used.
new_issues.why: True that `if context.params.get("system_prompt")` lets `system_prompt: ""` through. An empty per-step prompt is an edge input with no meaningful value to lose; falling back to the session prompt is not a material behavior error.

new_issues.title: dispatch_artifact appends the agent's final text to the error, which run.py prints inside Rich markup unescaped.
new_issues.why: True: the new code appends tail_text(response) to ActionResult.error, and run.py prints errors as rprint(f"[red]Error: {error_msg}[/red]"). Bracketed text in the tail is read as markup: it can drop tags like [x] or raise MarkupError on a stray closing tag such as a bracketed absolute path. The effect is limited to the end-of-run summary display after results are saved, and needs a specific bracket pattern in the last characters of the agent's text.
